facts.statement: Alxasaurus was discovered in 1988 during the China-Canada Dinosaur Project in the Bayin-Gobi Formation.
facts.quote: It is known from five specimens, recovered from the Bayin-Gobi in 1988, as part of the China-Canada Dinosaur Project.

facts.statement: The genus Alxasaurus was formally described and named in 1993 by paleontologists Dong Zhiming and Dale Russell.
facts.quote: In 1993, they described Alxasaurus and named its type species, A. elesitaiensis.

facts.statement: Alxasaurus lived during the Early Cretaceous (Albian age) in Inner Mongolia.
facts.quote: Alxasaurus (; meaning "Alxa lizard") is a genus of therizinosauroid theropod dinosaurs from the Early Cretaceous (Albian age) Bayin-Gobi Formation of Inner Mongolia.

facts.statement: Alxasaurus possessed an abbreviated tail, shortened metatarsals, broad feet, and long, recurved hand claws similar to derived therizinosaurs.
facts.quote: While outside of Therizinosauridae itself, Alxasaurus had many of the traits characteristic of derived therizinosaurs, such as an abbreviated tail, shortened metatarsals and broad feet convergent with those of basal sauropodomorphs, and fairly long, recurved hand claws.

facts.statement: Alxasaurus likely had a beak and a large gut, adaptations suited for a herbivorous diet.
facts.quote: Like related genera, it likely would have had a beak and a large gut, both adaptations for a herbivorous diet.

facts.statement: Russell and Dong estimated Alxasaurus to be 3.8 meters long, 1.5 meters high at the hip, and weigh 380 kg.
facts.quote: In 1993, Russell and Dong estimated a body length of 3.8 m, a hip height of 1.5 m, and a body mass of 380 kg.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul later estimated Alxasaurus to be 4 meters long and weigh 400 kg.
facts.quote: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated its length to be 4 m, and its body mass to be 400 kg.

facts.statement: The tooth-bearing part of the Alxasaurus dentary measured 18.5 cm in length.
facts.quote: The alveolar margin, the part of the dentary that bore teeth, measured 18.5 cm in length.

facts.statement: Although poorly preserved, evidence suggests Alxasaurus had interdental plates.
facts.quote: Though poorly preserved, interdental plates appear to have been present.

facts.statement: Alxasaurus had a tail that was short compared to other theropods.
facts.quote: The tail was short, relative to that of other theropods.

facts.statement: Alxasaurus had an abbreviated metatarsus, a trait convergent with basal sauropodomorphs.
facts.quote: The metatarsus overall was abbreviated, converging on basal sauropodomorphs.

facts.statement: The discovery of Alxasaurus supported the hypothesis that therizinosaurs were highly derived coelurosaurs rather than basal sauropodomorphs.
facts.quote: While therizinosaurs had previously been tentatively seen as late-surviving basal sauropodomorphs, the description of Alxasaurus lent credence to the idea that they were instead highly derived coelurosaurs.

facts.statement: The genus name Alxasaurus refers to the Alxa Desert in Inner Mongolia and the Greek word for lizard.
facts.quote: The genus is named after the Alxa Desert of Inner Mongolia, also known as the "Alashan" desert, and the name also includes the Greek word sauros ("lizard").

facts.statement: The species name elesitaiensis honors the village of Elesitai near the fossil discovery site.
facts.quote: The single known species, elesitaiensis, is named after Elesitai, a village found in this region, near which the fossil remains of Alxasaurus were located.

facts.statement: Alxasaurus claws were hollow near their base, a feature that contributed to their poor preservation.
facts.quote: The unguals (claws) were badly crushed, partly because they were hollow proximally.

facts.statement: Alxasaurus is classified within the family Alxasauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Alxasauridae

facts.statement: Alxasaurus belongs to the suborder Therizinosauria.
facts.quote: infraordo: Therizinosauria

facts.statement: Alxasaurus is a member of the order Saurischia.
facts.quote: ordo: Saurischia

facts.statement: Alxasaurus is classified under the suborder Theropoda.
facts.quote: subordo: Theropoda

facts.statement: The only known species of Alxasaurus is A. elesitaiensis.
facts.quote: species: A. elesitaiensis

facts.statement: The family Alxasauridae was created to include Alxasaurus but is considered of dubious utility because it contains only a single species.
facts.quote: Para incluirlo se ha creado una nueva familia llamada Alxasauridae, poco aceptada al incluir solo este género.

facts.statement: Alxasaurus was described and named by Chinese paleontologist Dong Zhiming and Canadian colleague Dale Russell in a 1993 publication.
facts.quote: Este dinosaurio fue descrito y nombrado por el paleontólogo chino, Dong Zhiming y su colega canadiense Dale Russell, en un trabajo publicado en 1993.

facts.statement: The name Alxasaurus is derived from the Alxa Desert in Inner Mongolia, China, combined with the Greek word sauros meaning "lizard".
facts.quote: Alxasaurus es nombrado por el Desierto de Alxa en la Mongolia Interior, también conocido como Desierto de Alashan junto con la palabra griega sauros ("lagarto").

facts.statement: The species name elesitaiensis honors the village of Elesitai, near where the fossils were found.
facts.quote: La única especie conocida, A. Elesitaiensis, se la nombra por la villa de Elesitai, cercana al lugar donde se encontraron los restos.

facts.statement: Five Alxasaurus skeletons were recovered from the Bayin Gobi Formation in Inner Mongolia.
facts.quote: Cinco esqueletos de Alxasaurus fueron recuperados de la formación Bayin-Gobi de Mongolia Interior

facts.statement: Alxasaurus lived during the mid-Cretaceous, approximately 100 million years ago in the Albian stage, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período geológico Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 100 millones de años, en el Albiense, en lo que hoy es Asia.

facts.statement: The fossils date to the Albian stage of the Early Cretaceous, approximately 112 to 100 million years ago.
facts.quote: que datan del Albiano durante en Cretácico inferior, aproximadamente 112 a 100 millones de años atrás.

facts.statement: Alxasaurus is one of the oldest members of the Therizinosauroidea superfamily but already possessed the body shape of later therizinosaurs, including a long neck, short tail, and large hand claws.
facts.quote: Es uno de los más antiguos miembros de la superfamilia Therizinosauroidea, pero que ya tenía la forma del cuerpo, incluyendo el cuello largo, la cola corta, y las garras grandes en las manos, de tericinosáuridos posteriores.

facts.statement: Alxasaurus was a bipedal herbivore with a large abdomen to house a complex digestive system for processing vegetation.
facts.quote: Como otros miembros de este grupo, era un herbívoro bípedo con una abdomen grande para contener el aparato digestivo para procesar los alimentos.

facts.statement: The largest known Alxasaurus specimen was about 4 meters long and 3 meters tall.
facts.quote: Con varios especímenes de alxasaurio conocidos, el más grande media alrededor de 4 metros de longitud y siendo bípedo, medía unos 3 m de altura.

facts.statement: According to Gregory S. Paul, Alxasaurus measured 4 meters in length and weighed approximately 400 kg.
facts.quote: De acuerdo con Gregory S. Paul, que era de 4 metros de largo y su peso fue de aproximadamente 400 kg.

facts.statement: Alxasaurus had enormous arms with long claws up to 40 cm, which it used to pull branches into its mouth.
facts.quote: Presentaba unos enormes brazos con largas garras, algunas de hasta 40 cm, que usaba para atraer las ramas a su boca.

facts.statement: Alxasaurus had a beak on its small head and about forty tiny teeth at the back of its mouth.
facts.quote: Poseía un pico en su pequeña cabeza, con unos cuarenta dientes diminutos en la parte posterior de la boca.

facts.statement: Due to its phylogenetic position, it is possible that Alxasaurus had feathers.
facts.quote: Por su posición filogénica es posible que tuviese plumas.

facts.statement: Alxasaurus possessed a semilunate carpal bone in its wrist, a feature found only in maniraptoran theropods like birds, dromaeosaurs, and troodontids.
facts.quote: Specifically, the semilunate carpal bone of the wrist is found only in maniraptoran theropods, which also include oviraptorosaurs, dromaeosaurs, troodontids, and birds.

facts.statement: While Alxasaurus exhibits typical therizinosaur features like body shape and teeth, its skeleton also demonstrates features present in more typical theropods.
facts.quote: Mientras que exhibe muchas características típicas de un tericinosáurido como la forma total del cuerpo y los dientes, el esqueleto de Alxasaurus también demuestra varias características presentes en terópodos más típicos
